seed_ledger.reason: No dedicated gas lateral found for the NextEra and Comstock plant near Bethel in Anderson County. A Comstock press release from March 2026 says the gas comes from the Western Haynesville, nearly 1 billion cubic feet a day by 2031, and points to transmission infrastructure at Bethel. A KLTV report on the April 2026 county commissioners meeting says there are no current data center plans and only a possible future tie. NextEra's April 2026 materials call the load a potential large industrial customer. A Standard and Poor's interview from September 2026 puts the plant next to the Trinity Gas Storage hub, but that page could not be read, so only its search summary was seen. No pipeline name, length or filing was found. The EIA pipeline projects table has no entry for Anderson County. A search of federal prior notice filings found nothing for the county. Searches run: 11. Sources checked: Comstock press release, KLTV, Data Center Dynamics on the NextEra federal approval, Natural Gas Intelligence, Utility Dive, Oil and Gas Journal on the Comstock midstream deal, Standard and Poor's summary, the EIA table, a FERC filing search, and a Railroad Commission search, which showed no T-4 or tap filing.

No gas supplier or pipeline named for the Pampa plant in Gray County. APR Energy cites local gas access and on-site modular turbines for 400 megawatts, with room to grow. A separate Duos Technologies plan at the same industrial park would self-generate 500 megawatts. A trade report says Elon Musk bought APR, so the project's status is unclear. The Natural Gas Pipeline of America line is about 1.5 km away but no tie was found. No county record, air permit, FERC filing or EIA project entry was found. Searches run: 10. Sources checked: Data Center Dynamics on the APR approval, Data Center Dynamics on Duos, a KFDA and NewsChannel 10 report on the nearby Google data center, a trade report on the APR sale, an air permit search, the EIA table, and a FERC filing search, which each showed nothing tied to the plant.

No gas supplier or lateral named for the Jarrell campus. The Mesone data center at 3911 County Road 305 was annexed and rezoned by the city in October 2025. The developers are Prominent Property Group, Savannah Developers and Power Infrastructure Partners, and they say the site would have 200 megawatts from gas and grid power. The Williamson County Sun said in April 2026 that utility agreements were not final. A broker listing for a different parcel at 4801 County Road 239 says two large interstate lines cross it and talks with both operators are underway, but it names neither operator and is not tied to this plant. The EIA table has no Williamson County entry, and searches for city agendas, air permits, the Railroad Commission and FERC filings found nothing. Searches run: 9. Sources checked: Texas Scorecard, Data Center Dynamics on the approval and on the opposition, the Williamson County Sun, broker listings, the city calendar, and the filing searches named above.
